cards.text: Paul is a prisoner, and he has appealed to Caesar (Acts 25:11). Now it's decided: Paul and some other prisoners are going to sail for Italy. Friend, this is one trip where you do NOT get to pick your seat.

cards.question: Paul and the other prisoners need someone to guard them on the trip to Italy. Who are they handed over to?

cards.text: They board a ship from Adramyttium, bound for ports along the coast of Asia, and put out to sea. The writer of Acts keeps saying 'we,' so he's ON this boat, friend, and so is Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica.
The next day they land at Sidon. Paul's still a prisoner, and Julius the centurion is the man holding the keys.

cards.question: True or false: At Sidon, Julius the centurion lets Paul go visit his friends and receive their care.

cards.text: Out of Sidon they go, but they don't sail straight across. They sail to the lee of Cyprus.

cards.question: Leaving Sidon, they sail to the lee of Cyprus because the ___ are against them.

cards.text: They cross the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and come to Myra in Lycia. Cilicia, Pamphylia, Lycia… friend, I can't say those three in a row without spitting cookie dough on the counter.

cards.question: Their first ship was only sailing for ports along the coast of Asia. At Myra, Julius finds a new ship sailing for Italy and puts them on board. Where is that ship from?

cards.text: It's slow sailing for many days, and when the wind gets in the way off Cnidus, they slip down to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone. Friend, that's rush hour on the water: creep forward a little, then sit there FOREVER.

cards.question: True or false: Once they're moving along the coast of Crete, the sailing finally gets easy.

cards.text: They finally pull into a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea. By now a lot of time has passed, and since it's after the Fast, the voyage has gotten dangerous.

cards.question: With the voyage getting dangerous, Paul speaks up at Fair Havens. What does Paul warn the men he can see coming?

answers.text: Disaster and great loss even of their lives
Pirates waiting for them along the coast
A sickness spreading among the prisoners

cards.question: True or false: Julius the centurion goes along with Paul's advice.
Instead of listening to Paul, Julius is persuaded by the ship's ___ and the ship's ___.
Most of the men want to leave Fair Havens and sail on. Why?

answers.text: The harbor isn't good for spending winter
The town of Lasea won't let them stay
Paul tells them the weather will hold

cards.question: The majority hope they can somehow reach a harbor called ___ and spend the winter there.

cards.text: A gentle south wind starts to blow, and they figure this is their chance, so they weigh anchor and sail along, hugging the coast of Crete. Nice and gentle, friend, so enjoy it while it lasts.

cards.question: Not long after they leave, that gentle south wind is gone. What sweeps down across the island of Crete?

answers.text: A hailstorm like the one in Egypt
A whirlwind out of the desert

cards.text: The ship can't head into the wind, so they quit fighting it and let themselves be driven along. Friend, that was me every time somebody yanked open the junk drawer: no steering, just SLIDING.

cards.question: True or false: Passing the small island of Cauda in the storm, they get the lifeboat secured with no trouble at all.
Once the lifeboat is hoisted up, what does the crew do to the ship next?

answers.text: They pass ropes under the ship
They nail extra boards on the ship
They tie the ship to the lifeboat

cards.text: Afraid of running aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lower the sea anchor, and the next day, tossed hard by the storm, the men start throwing the cargo overboard. Somebody's delivery is NOT showing up on time.
On the third day, they throw the ship's tackle overboard with their own hands. Friend, when the crew starts tossing the ship's OWN gear, I'd be hugging the nearest post.
For many days, neither sun nor stars appear, and the great storm keeps battering them. No stars for DAYS? Friend, lighting stars is my whole night shift, and I'm sweating just hearing this.

cards.question: With no sun or stars for many days and the storm still battering the ship, what happens to the men's hope?

answers.text: They lose all hope of being saved
They still hope to reach Phoenix
They hope Julius will find a way

cards.text: The men have gone a long time without food. Then Paul stands up right in the middle of them.

cards.question: Standing among the men in the storm, Paul starts by bringing up what happened back at Crete. What does Paul say?

answers.text: They should have taken his advice and stayed
They should have waited for a better wind
They should have found a bigger ship there

cards.text: Friend, that's a holy 'I told you so,' and I respect it. But then Paul turns right around and urges them to keep up their courage.

cards.question: True or false: Paul tells the men that some of them will lose their lives in this storm.
Paul tells the men the only loss will be the ___.

cards.text: Paul says that just last night, an angel of the God he belongs to and serves stood beside him. Friend, an angel showed up at my junk drawer once, and trust me, you do NOT forget that.

cards.question: The angel tells Paul not to be afraid. What does the angel say Paul must do?

answers.text: Go back to his friends in Sidon

cards.question: The angel tells Paul that God has granted him the lives of ___ who sail with him.

cards.text: Then Paul tells the men, "So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me." A whole ship out of hope, and one prisoner standing there believing God.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the ship will reach safety without ever running aground.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this voyage is NOT over.
